narrative:
The model determined that you have a 90.8% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the law school sets a high bar for admission and wants students likely to succeed, this strong prediction of failure led to your application being rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. Your first-year and third-year class rankings had the greatest influence. Being in the bottom decile for grades in both Year 1 and Year 3 strongly pushed the model toward predicting failure, as these rankings are far below the average of accepted students (around the 6th and 5.8th deciles respectively). Your LSAT score was the third most important factor and also pulled the prediction toward failure. At 27, it sits well below the average of 37 among accepted applicants.

These academic performance signals outweighed other details such as your middle family income bracket, 3.2 undergraduate GPA (nearly identical to the accepted average), full-time study plans, gender, and race, none of which played a role in the outcome.

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance and retaking the LSAT to reach a score closer to the mid-30s or higher. Strengthening these key areas will directly address what the model saw as your biggest risks. Consider additional bar exam preparation resources or academic support programs before reapplying. prompt:
A machine learning model predicted that a student will FAIL the bar exam and therefore their application for university admission was REJECTED. Your goal is to generate an explanatory narrative based on the information provided (1-5), explaining why the law school application was denied for this student.

1. DATASET INFORMATION
The dataset contains information on students who took the bar exam.

The target variable is whether the student passed the bar exam on the first try (0 = passed, 1 = failed).

Protected attributes gender and race were not used to make the machine prediction.

2. TECHNICAL EXPLANATION: SHAP VALUES
A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward "will fail" (bar exam failure), negative toward "will pass" (bar exam success). Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.

3. STUDENT PROFILE 
You are writing a narrative tailored to this specific person who is rejected law school admission.

- gender = male (the gender of the student.)

- Predicted probability of failure: 90.8%

Write a detailed narrative explanation tailored to this non-technical reader that MUST explain:
